JUMP-EN035, distributed as a Shonen Jump subscription bonus from the March 2010 issue; before EdisonFormat.com's promo cutoff (latest legal JUMP promo: Cyber Eltanin, JUMP-EN038). Our product date is year-precision, hence the explicit include. YGOPRODeck's Edison pool includes it.

exclude.reason: JUMP-EN039, the Shonen Jump May 2010 issue promo. THE COMMUNITY FORMAT AND THE HISTORICAL EVENT DIVERGE HERE, deliberately preserved on the community side (this pool's legality_basis is community-retrospective): EdisonFormat.com defines the latest legal JUMP promo as Cyber Eltanin (JUMP-EN038) and both independent community pools exclude Hundred Eyes Dragon - but Konami's own FAQ for the 75th SJC (captured 2010-04-11) answered 'What cards are legal for play?' with SHONEN JUMP promos 'up until Hundred Eyes Dragon', i.e. the card WAS legal at SJC Edison itself (the May cover issue shipped in April). A future historical-event pool would include it. Its month-precision date straddles the 2010-05-10 cutoff, hence the explicit entry.

region_substitutions.reason: TDGS-EN016's release printing resolves to 96782886, BabelCDB's canonical (alias=0) row for Mind Master - but that row is scoped SCOPE_OCG-only (ot=1). BabelCDB ships the TCG-text printing as a separate row, 96782896 (cards-unofficial.cdb, ot=2 SCOPE_TCG, alias=96782886), placed exactly +10 from the base - outside EDOPro's <10 artwork-auto-extension window (IsInArtworkOffsetRange), so it does not inherit the base row's whitelist entry and must be listed explicitly. A TCG-format pool referencing 96782886 is a passcode an EDOPro official-cards room (TCG) would reject; 96782896 is the region- and text-correct identity for this printing. The banlist's own Mind Master entry is left citing 96782886 unchanged (see retroformats/lflist.py's region_substitution_origin bridge) rather than rewritten.

exclude_products.reason: The format is defined as ending 2010-05-10, the day before The Shining Darkness's NORTH AMERICAN release; both dates are period-verified against archived 2010 Konami product pages (NA Launch/Tournament Legal Date 5/11/10; Europe 05/07/10). The EU street date falls inside the window but the set is outside the format: EdisonFormat.com's set list stops at Duelist Pack: Kaiba and no community implementation includes TSHD cards.

Distributed at TSHD Sneak Peek events - per archived official pages these ran 2010-05-01/02 in NA/LatAm and 2010-04-30..05-02 in Europe (correcting an earlier assumption of May 8-9), nominally inside the cutoff window and after SJC Edison (April 24-25). The community format excludes it: EdisonFormat.com's set list omits it and both independent community pools exclude XX-Saber Boggart Knight. The event's own FAQ (captured 2010-04-11) predates the Sneak Peek and does not list it either.

PERIOD POLICY, not merely community convention: Konami's own rule throughout 2009-2010 was that Duel Terminal machine-exclusive cards were NOT legal in sanctioned play until released in another product (stated in premier-event FAQs from mid-2009, in Kevin Tewart's official strategy-site article of 2010-03-19 - before SJC Edison - and enumerated card-by-card in the June 2010 US WCQ FAQ; the SJC Edison FAQ itself lists the illegal Duel Terminal exclusives). Reprints inside DT sets were legal through their original products, which this product-level exclusion preserves. EdisonFormat.com's set list and both independent community pools agree.

JUMP-EN041/EN042 are after the community format's promo cutoff (latest legal JUMP promo: Cyber Eltanin, JUMP-EN038, per EdisonFormat.com); both community pools exclude The Tyrant Neptune and Transforming Sphere. Note the deliberate divergence documented on the Hundred Eyes Dragon exclusion: the historical event's own FAQ set the boundary one promo later.
Tyler the Great Warrior (TYL-EN001) is a one-of-one charity card; it was never obtainable or sanctioned for tournament play and appears in no Edison pool reference.

notes: LEGALITY BASIS community-retrospective: this pool reproduces the modern community's Edison Format convention (EdisonFormat.com's definition and its linked references), anchored to but distinct from what was registerable at SJC Edison on 2010-04-24 - the one documented divergence (Hundred Eyes Dragon, legal at the event per Konami's own FAQ, excluded by the community convention) is recorded on its exclusion entry. Materialised from data/releases/ under certified coverage: every card whose earliest TCG release event (any TCG territory) is on or before 2010-05-10, with five sourced product exclusions and three sourced promo boundary resolutions. VERIFIED status earned 2026-08-20 under the strict vocabulary: (1) internally complete and cross-checked against two independent community pools (YGOPRODeck Edison tag - every reference card present, our 15 extras all confirmed pre-cutoff printings its tag wrongly omits - and the termitaklk whitelist); (2) coverage certified through the gap ledger (data/releases/gaps.json - the 2026-08 certification pass accounted for all 45 importer-detected anomalies across 23 gap records, each resolved with evidence, mechanically recomputed where checkable; the validator keeps the ledger exhaustive thereafter); (3) the load-bearing historical claims corroborated by period primary sources: all five boundary product dates verified against archived 2010 Konami product pages, the Duel Terminal exclusion verified against Konami's 2009-2010 tournament policy, and the promo boundary anchored to the archived SJC Edison FAQ. Known deliberate deviation from the references: Royal Knight of the Ice Barrier (Duel Terminal-only) stays excluded - now backed by period policy, which made DT-machine exclusives illegal in sanctioned play; the references include it while excluding every other DT01-only card. Europe-only products (Retro Pack, GX Tag Force 3) are IN via all-TCG territory scoping - period-corroborated: UDE policy made TCG legality worldwide-simultaneous, and Konami-era event FAQs explicitly listed the GX Tag Force 3 promos as legal at US premier events.
